records.description: Reduce bovine pancreatic RNase with mercaptoethanol in 8 M urea; remove reagents by Sephadex G25. Adjust the resulting reduced-chain preparation to pH 8.2 with tris-acetate and oxidize in open beakers at 23-24 C at 2.0 or 0.1 mg/ml. Follow SH disappearance by p-chloromercuribenzoate and radiolabeled iodoacetate, optical rotation at 366 nm and UV spectra. Acidified aliquots are assayed at pH 5 against RNA and separately uridylic-2-prime,3-prime-cyclic phosphate with native-enzyme controls.

records.description: Use purified mature DM-MBP V8G/Y283D, normally100 nM at 25 C, plus concentration-series and wild-type controls. The chloride-containing arm dilutes100-fold from 6 M guanidine-HCl into 20 mM Tris-HCl pH7.5,200 mM KCl and 5 mM Mg(OAc)2. The chloride-deficient arm dilutes100-fold from 9.5 M urea into 100 mM Hepes pH7.5,20 mM KOAc and 5 mM Mg(OAc)2. In each chaperonin arm capture with 250 nM GroEL or SR1, then add 250 nM GroES and 5 mM ATP. Record tryptophan fluorescence at 295 nm excitation/345 nm emission and separate dynamic light scattering. The two solution protocols differ in several components.
records.name: Purified DM-MBP refolding and aggregation context
openObligations: Purified, already synthesized clients and purified E. coli GroEL/SR1/GroES are studied in vitro. The selected data do not observe translation, cellular stress adaptation, protein damage surveillance, routing to proteasomes or organismal proteome reliability.

Adding the GroEL/GroES/ATP protocol is a combined intervention. These panels do not by themselves isolate ATP hydrolysis, individual ATPase steps, capture specificity, every component necessity or all possible active folding effects.

Activity recovery, tryptophan fluorescence, light scattering and size-exclusion elution measure different properties. None alone supplies an atomic native structure, a unique folding path or the fraction of every chain in a single native state.
All readouts and fitted rates come from one publication. No raw traces, new fit, covariance, curve digitization, independent replication or analytically-checked status is supplied.

The source interprets these conditions through aggregation prevention. Its broad passive-cage conclusion is retained as conditional, not a proof that all chaperonins are passive or that no client can experience an active conformational effect.

The DM-MBP client is mature V8G/Y283D maltose-binding protein. Tryptophan fluorescence is an environment-sensitive refolding proxy; no maltose-binding affinity, transport activity or enzymatic client assay is measured here.

The chloride-containing protocol uses 20 mM Tris-HCl pH7.5,200 mM KCl and 5 mM Mg(OAc)2 after dilution from 6 M guanidine-HCl. The chloride-deficient protocol uses 100 mM Hepes pH7.5,20 mM KOAc and 5 mM Mg(OAc)2 after dilution from 9.5 M urea. Buffer, salt concentration/anion and starting denaturant all change; chloride alone is not isolated.

Concentration dependence and light scattering support intermolecular association under the tested solution protocol. They do not identify a unique oligomer structure or prove that every fluorescence intermediate is an aggregate.

Rate equivalence in the changed solution protocol constrains a need for a faster intrinsic cage-only step for this client under those conditions. It does not prove an unchanged microscopic route or universal absence of chaperonin active effects.

openObligations: The existing reviewed positive case concerns highly ionized stored 140Pr charge states in a high-vacuum storage ring, not biochemical coordination, enzymes, cells or a matched chemical intervention. The original theoretical and empirical placeholders have null DOI and Link. They identify no biochemical isotope, substrate or enzyme preparation, decay-channel readout, comparison or uncertainty model. The asserted chemical/enzymatic experimental support is excluded from this admission; the broader biochemical dependence remains explicitly unsupported here.

This is a statement about what the present review has admitted. No comprehensive search of chemical or biochemical electron-capture literature has been performed, and no absence of such effects throughout the literature or in nature is asserted.

Electronic occupancy, electron density at the nucleus, nuclear/electronic angular momentum and state populations are distinct dependencies. The selected Pr140 H-like/He-like contrast does not supply a universal electron-density coefficient or monotonic electron-count law. A biochemical binding-context mechanism would require its own specified channel and comparison.

The source does not demonstrate altered underlying nuclear forces or an enzyme-catalyzed nuclear reaction. Ionization preserves which parent isotope is prepared; the subsequent EC transition changes the nuclear charge and element. Do not inherit the original parent prose as nuclear identity invariance through decay.

Original parent 2.18 has a finite isotope- and channel-specific disposition. Its necessary label, weight 1.0, CausalDirections [1], InteractionModes [1], DependencyType 10 and OntologicalRole arising do not establish a biochemical causal relation or downward-causation mechanism.

The original carrier group 1/type 1, N_min=N_crit=1 and N_sat=null are catalogue codes, not a calibrated nuclear-particle or biochemical threshold. No replacement minimum or operational carrier count is inferred.

Level 3, Phase 2, TypeRole 3 Property, Science [1,2,3], hypothesized status and Requirements MustCover [0,10], ShouldCover [4,12], OptionalCover [5,7] are draft classification and coverage choices. They establish no measured formation stage, persistent biological property, material resource threshold or universal hierarchy.

A stronger admission would need an identified isotope and EC channel, a specified biochemical/electronic preparation and matched control, a channel-specific rate observable with background/loss separation, and stated inference uncertainties. Those are open obligations rather than results of the current ion experiment.

limitations: Boots FRET uses chemically synthesized Cy3/Cy5-labelled complexes with a deoxy cleavage-site substrate, at about 25 nM complex. Main cleavage kinetics use mostly T7-transcribed cleavable RNA at 0.5-1 micromolar ribozyme with a 10:1 strand ratio. They are linked but distinct preparations, not simultaneous structure and chemistry of one molecule.

The I-II dye pair reports global stem proximity. The source explicitly says it cannot establish formation of the specific loop-loop tertiary contact or a unique catalytically active local conformation.

Source two-state/Hill assumptions may not hold microscopically; fitted midpoints compare empirical global-folding responses rather than determine metal-binding mechanisms, microscopicKD or bound-ion counts. n less than 1 is not a fractional ion molecule count.

The labelled construct was selected because its fast-population kobs agreed with unlabelled RNA, reported as data not shown. Chemically synthesized and transcribed strands nevertheless have different cleavage plateaus, so equality of the fast rate does not validate equality of active fractions.

Replacing loop II with UUCG changes the donor position as well as possible tertiary interaction. Different FRET amplitudes cannot alone quantify the same distance or population change across these variants.
The four-ion FRET comparison coversCa, Mg, Mn and Sr. Co, Zn andCd are excluded because of optical interference or solubility; no absent FRET result is filled in from the kinetic series.

Source dye-only controls showed Mn quenching above 10 mM; the source applied a linear correction, about 10% at 60 mM. Raw spectra/corrections were not independently replayed. High-salt and high-ion conditions are in vitro regimes rather than whole-cell measurements.
